source: The last submit_thesis call of three Writer runs that saved nothing (2026-11-10 and 2026-11-13), verbatim from each run's saved thread, which holds the call as the SDK's parse returned it (a filing's type in `variable`; the model wrote it in `value`); the live price each run pulled; HTFL's thesis, passed 2026-08-20.

decision.conviction_rationale: The de-risking on the extension reason is real and materially changes the setup from the October drop. But this remains a first-approval binary on a drug in a rare pediatric population where pivotal data comes from a small registrational cohort, the stock has already recovered 37% off the low, and I'm entering above the current price on a reclaim — I won't have the position if the run-up doesn't start. The target at the August 52-week high of $392.70 is about 11% above entry, against a 33% stop distance — under 2×, which I would normally flag as marginal, but the actual plan is to exit before the event in December, not at the target, and the event premium should carry the stock well above $392 if approval sentiment builds. I am using the 52-week high as a trim trigger, not a destination.
decision.core_belief: Praxis is a late-stage CNS company with two drugs under FDA review — relutrigine for a rare pediatric epilepsy with no approved treatment and ulixacaltamide for essential tremor, the most common movement disorder with no disease-specific therapy. Both carry Breakthrough Therapy Designation, the commercial team for relutrigine is already fully hired, and $1.3B in cash funds the company into 2028 past both decisions. What has to stay true: the FDA review proceeds to a standard approval on December 27 with no further amendments or CMC surprises.
invalidation_conditions: A new 8-K from Praxis announcing a second PDUFA extension or a Complete Response Letter for relutrigine at any point before December 27 — this would immediately break the core belief.
A complete response letter or unexpected rejection on ulixacaltamide (January 29 PDUFA) that calls into question the FDA's posture toward the company's data package broadly.
The stock fails to close above $351.64 by December 6 — meaning the run-up never started — at which point the setup has failed on its own terms and the entry is set down.
key_assumptions: Relutrigine's NDA review proceeds on the December 27 schedule with no further major amendments or additional FDA information requests — monitored continuously via any PRAX 8-K filing before December 27.

The sensitivity analyses that triggered the extension were consistent with the primary EMBOLD efficacy result and do not reveal ambiguity that would prompt a Complete Response Letter — checked at the December 27 decision date.
Cash of $1.3B as of September 30, 2026 funds operations into 2028 without a dilutive raise ahead of the approval — checked at the Q4 2026 report, expected in February 2027.
decision.rationale: Praxis fell 6% today with the broader healthcare selloff — no company-specific news behind it. The investor day this morning was straightforwardly positive: fully hired field team for relutrigine, sensitivity analyses for both drugs consistent with primary results, and $1.3B in cash past the decision dates. The PDUFA extension question — the original reason the prior thesis was dropped at low conviction — is answered: it was a data submission classified as a major amendment, with no new trials required and no safety concerns raised. The 44-day window to December 27 is squarely where I'd be building a position, but the stock has already run 37% off the October low, so I want to see it reclaim the 20-day high of $351.64 on a close before entering — that confirms the run-up is actually starting rather than stalling. I'm proposing the entry at $351.65 on a close, stop under the October swing low at $236.79 (advisory — gap risk on a binary means size is the real control), and an exit 1–2 weeks before December 27, around December 6–13. The Street's average target of $728 sits 107% above the entry level, against a 33% distance to the structural stop; the wide analyst spread ($343–$1,201 low to high) reflects real uncertainty on approval odds, not just valuation. I'd size near the low end of the band given the binary nature, and I'd be out before the decision regardless of where the stock is.
decision.stop_basis: A close below $236.79 — the October 14 swing low — would mean the market has re-priced the approval probability sharply lower, likely on a new FDA communication or a peer CRL in a related indication; it breaks the core belief that the review is proceeding cleanly. The stop sits under the October swing low, the only structural level below the base. At 5.6% ATR and a binary event, this stop is advisory — a CRL gap would skip straight through it, which is why position size (at the low end of the band) is the primary risk control here, not the stop distance.
decision.target_basis: No price target is set for the run-up version of this trade — the exit is time-based, not price-based: I plan to sell 1–2 weeks before December 27, in the December 6–13 window, whatever the price. The Street's average target of $728 and low of $343 bracket a wide range of approval-scenario outcomes; I am not pricing the approval, only the pre-decision run. The target_price is set at $392.70 (the 52-week high and the August peak), which serves as a natural trim point if reached; the December review trigger is the primary exit signal.

triggers.rationale: A close above the 20-day high of $351.64 confirms the run-up is starting rather than stalling — this is the RECLAIM entry the setup requires, and I want confirmation on the close, not an intraday poke.
Any red-tier filing from Praxis — flag immediately in case it is an FDA communication, a PDUFA update, or anything that changes the December 27 timeline or the safety picture.
Flag seven days before the next earnings report so I can decide whether to trim before the print — a quarterly update this close to the PDUFA could move the stock sharply either way.
Flag 23 days after the December 27 event date — the latest this position should be open is T+30; if still held, I exit or reassess at this point.

decision.variant_view: The Street is pricing PRAX as a near-coin-flip binary despite the fact that the PDUFA extension was caused by Praxis itself submitting additional supportive data — not by an FDA information request or a safety signal. That's a meaningfully different risk profile than the market treated it as when the stock sold from $390 to $237. With no advisory committee and sensitivity analyses confirmed consistent with primary results, this reads more like a de-risked regulatory step than a first-approval gamble. Analysts expect a 50/50 binary; I think the approval probability is higher, and the recent price recovery has not fully closed that gap.

decision.conviction_rationale: The business quality is HIGH — demand exceeds supply through 2027, margins are improving, and the company just turned its first GAAP profit. The stock is LOW: it's in a confirmed downtrend, 78% off its high, with no base and no rising averages to buy against. The Street's average target of $111.25 is 122% above the current price, with the high at $165 — the upside is real if the chart repairs, but I won't price a plan against a falling knife. Medium conviction reflects genuine belief in the company and no confidence in the entry timing yet.
decision.core_belief: Applied Optoelectronics is the only large-scale U.S.-based maker of 800G and 1.6T fiber-optic transceivers for AI data centers, a position that earns it pricing power and preferred-supplier status at a moment when hyperscalers are expanding faster than the supply chain can keep up. The company just returned to GAAP profitability with revenue growing 128% year over year, backed by a $1–$1.5B three-year supply agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscaler — what has to stay true is that DSP component supply improves in early 2027, allowing the company to ship into its $450M backlog of 1.6T orders, and that AI data center spending doesn't pause long enough to let inventory build.
invalidation_conditions: Q4 2026 revenue comes in below the low end of guidance ($385M), signaling the DSP constraint is worse than management said, checked at the February 25, 2027 earnings report
Management cuts or withdraws the 2027 capacity build plan, signaling the AI demand cycle is softening faster than the supply ramp — checked in each quarterly filing and transcript
The hyperscaler LTA is terminated or materially amended on supply-failure grounds, disclosed via 8-K
key_assumptions: DSP component availability improves substantially in Q1 2027 as management guided, allowing shipments against the $450M 1.6T order backlog — checked at the Q4 2026 earnings report expected February 25, 2027
Q4 2026 revenue comes in at or above the guided midpoint of $402.5M, confirming the capacity ramp is on track — checked at the Q4 2026 report on February 25, 2027
The Tier 1 hyperscaler LTA remains in force with no supply-condition breach, confirmed in each 10-Q filing
decision.rationale: Applied Optoelectronics reported Q3 on November 5 with an EPS beat and a revenue beat, but Q4 revenue guidance came in at $385M–$420M, a midpoint of $402.5M that missed Street consensus of $427.3M — that's a guidance miss, not a raise, so the post-earnings drift setup doesn't qualify. The stock dropped 10% in after-hours on the print, then recovered 4.5% the next session on only 1.6× average volume: neither the volume nor the gap direction matches a clean signal. The chart reinforces the pass: a confirmed downtrend, price 32% below a falling 20-day average, Trend Template scoring 3 of 8. The business case is real — first GAAP profit, demand sold out through 2027, a $1B–$1.5B hyperscaler supply agreement — but a great company in a broken chart is a watch. I'm saving this LONG and WATCHING, with a review trigger when price reclaims the 20-day moving average; that's where I'd price an entry plan.

triggers.rationale: Price has climbed back to the falling 20-day average around $73.70 — this is where I'd look at an entry plan. If the 20-day has also started turning up and volume is healthy, the pullback setup becomes live; send it for a decision.

Q4 2026 earnings are expected around February 25, 2027 — flag this a week ahead so I can check whether the DSP constraint eased and whether the Q4 revenue number landed at or above $402.5M, the two things that would change the entry call.
AAOI has filed five major-agreement 8-Ks since August — any new material agreement filing could signal another hyperscaler deal or a change to the existing LTA, both of which would update the thesis.

decision.variant_view: Analysts treat the Q4 guidance miss as a supply-timing problem; I think it is also a credibility test — management has now guided below consensus twice in a row while blaming DSP shortages, and the market won't re-rate the stock until it sees a quarter where supply actually catches demand. The business is as good as bulls say; the stock needs an execution proof before it earns a re-entry.

add_triggers.rationale: HeartFlow is approaching the rising 50-day average — the level where a pullback buy plan would be valid. Flag to check whether the pullback came on light volume and whether the stock is holding the average before writing a priced entry.

decision.conviction_rationale: The business is excellent — revenue accelerating for three straight quarters, 83%+ gross margins, reimbursement now covering ~75% of insured lives, and losses narrowing fast. But the stock sold off on a strong beat, analyst targets average $48.50 against a $60 price (meaning the Street hasn't repriced up yet, not that upside is wide), and no revisions followed. I'd own this in a pullback setup but won't chase it here.
decision.core_belief: HeartFlow is the category leader in AI-powered coronary artery disease diagnostics, with two reimbursed products on a platform validated in over 100 clinical studies. Revenue is growing at 50%+ with 83%+ gross margins, payer coverage is now broad enough to support routine clinical use, and the company is on a credible path to cash flow profitability by mid-2028. What has to stay true is that coronary CT scan volumes keep growing, Plaque Analysis adoption continues to scale, and no major payer pulls coverage.
invalidation_conditions: Revenue growth decelerates below 30% year-over-year in any reported quarter, suggesting the acceleration thesis is broken — checked at each earnings report.

A major national payer (UnitedHealth, Cigna, Aetna, or CMS) reverses or restricts coverage for Plaque Analysis, reducing the addressable reimbursement base — watched for in 8-K filings and press releases at any time.
key_assumptions: FFRct and Plaque Analysis case volume continues growing above 50% year-over-year, sustaining revenue acceleration — checked at the Q4 2026 earnings report, expected in February 2027.
Payer coverage for Plaque Analysis holds at or above 75% of insured U.S. lives with no material coverage reversals — checked in each 10-Q filing and any 8-K disclosing payer policy changes.
Non-GAAP operating losses continue to narrow toward the mid-2028 profitability target, with no need for a dilutive equity raise — checked at the Q4 2026 report and in the annual 10-K.
decision.rationale: HeartFlow reported a strong Q3 yesterday — revenue up 57% and a material guidance raise — but the stock fell about 5% on the print and is only now recovering. My strategy's clearest rule is that a beat the market sells is a fade signal, not a buy. The EPS beat was real (71% above estimates), the guidance raise was real ($15M above the prior midpoint), and the business is genuinely accelerating — but zero analyst revisions have followed in the 72 hours since the print, and the gap-day action went the wrong direction. All three post-earnings drift entry conditions fail: the stock did not gap up, the gap-day close was not in the upper half of the range, and no estimate revision momentum has appeared. The business deserves owning; the setup today does not. If HeartFlow pulls back to the rising 50-day around $52 on light volume and holds, that is where the pullback plan gets written — buy at the average, stop about one normal daily move below it.
decision.variant_view: Analysts have an average price target of $48.50 against a stock trading at nearly $60, implying the Street thinks the stock is overpriced. I think they are simply behind: guidance now implies full-year revenue of $263M against a prior consensus of $248M, and if Plaque Analysis continues scaling into a $36–37M run-rate product with 83%+ margins, the 2027 revenue number could be materially above where models sit today. The stock isn't cheap, but the Street's targets were written before this guidance raise.
